questions.prompt: Why use a Route 53 alias record instead of a CNAME for a load balancer?
options: It works at the zone apex and costs nothing to resolve
questions.explanation: A CNAME cannot exist at the root of a domain, and alias queries to AWS targets are not charged.

questions.prompt: Which routing policy sends traffic to a backup only when the primary fails?
questions.explanation: Failover routing uses health checks to switch to the secondary record.

questions.prompt: What does a launch template define?
options: The configuration used when launching an instance
questions.explanation: It captures the AMI, type, security groups, user data and other launch settings in one reusable object.

questions.prompt: What do minimum, maximum and desired capacity control in an Auto Scaling group?
options: The lower bound, upper bound and current target number of instances
questions.explanation: Desired is what it aims for now, while minimum and maximum are the boundaries it will never cross.

questions.prompt: What happens when you manually terminate an instance in an Auto Scaling group?
questions.explanation: Self healing is one of the main reasons to use an Auto Scaling group at all.

questions.prompt: Why is running two instances in the same availability zone not high availability?
options: A single zone failure takes both of them down
questions.explanation: The zone is the shared point of failure, so redundancy inside it does not protect you.

questions.prompt: What does an RDS Multi AZ standby do?
options: Sits ready to take over on failover
questions.explanation: The standby is not readable, and its job is availability rather than scaling reads.

questions.prompt: What is a read replica used for?
options: Serving read queries to reduce load on the primary
questions.explanation: Replicas scale read capacity, which is a different problem from failover.

questions.prompt: When would you choose a Network Load Balancer over an Application Load Balancer?
options: For very high throughput at layer four or non HTTP protocols
questions.explanation: The NLB works at the transport layer and handles extreme throughput and non HTTP traffic.

questions.prompt: What does path based routing on an ALB let you do?
options: Send different URL paths to different target groups
questions.explanation: One load balancer can front several services by matching on the request path.

questions.prompt: Why do sticky sessions limit scaling?
options: Requests are tied to one instance, so load spreads unevenly
questions.explanation: Pinning a user to one target undermines the even distribution a load balancer exists to provide.

questions.prompt: What is a Route 53 health check used for?
options: Deciding whether a record should receive traffic
questions.explanation: Health checks feed routing decisions, which is what makes failover routing work.

questions.prompt: Auto Scaling groups can span multiple availability zones.
questions.explanation: Spreading across zones is exactly how they provide resilience to a zone failure.

questions.prompt: A target tracking scaling policy adds and removes instances to hold a metric near a target value.
questions.explanation: You state the target, such as average CPU, and the group adjusts capacity to keep it there.

questions.prompt: Load balancer access logs can be delivered to an S3 bucket for later analysis.
questions.explanation: Enabling them gives you a record of every request that reached the balancer.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of CloudFront in front of an origin?
options: Lower latency for users and less load on the origin
questions.explanation: Content served from an edge location is closer to the user and never touches the origin.

questions.prompt: You changed a file but CloudFront still serves the old one. What do you do?
options: Invalidate the cache or use a new object name
questions.explanation: Cached copies persist until they expire, so you invalidate or version the object name.

questions.prompt: Why lock an S3 bucket so it is reachable only through CloudFront?
options: So users cannot bypass the cache and hit the origin directly
questions.explanation: Direct access defeats both the caching and any rules you enforce at the edge.

questions.prompt: Which storage option can be mounted by several instances at once?
questions.explanation: EFS is a shared network filesystem, while an EBS volume attaches to one instance at a time.

questions.prompt: When is S3 the right choice over EBS?
options: For objects like backups, images and static assets
questions.explanation: Object storage suits whole files accessed by key, not block level reads and writes.

questions.prompt: What does an S3 lifecycle rule do?
options: Moves or expires objects automatically based on age
questions.explanation: Lifecycle rules are the main tool for controlling long term storage cost.

questions.prompt: What is the trade off with archive storage classes?
options: Much lower cost but slower retrieval
questions.explanation: You accept a retrieval delay in exchange for a large reduction in storage price.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between durability and availability?
options: Durability is not losing data, availability is being able to reach it
questions.explanation: Data can be perfectly durable and still be temporarily unreachable.

questions.prompt: What does encryption in transit protect against?
options: Someone reading traffic on the network path
questions.explanation: It protects data while it moves, which is a different problem from protecting it at rest.

questions.prompt: What controls who can use a KMS key?
options: The key policy and IAM permissions
questions.explanation: The key policy is authoritative, and locking yourself out of it is a real risk.

questions.prompt: When would DynamoDB suit a workload better than RDS?
options: Simple key based access at very high scale
questions.explanation: Key value access patterns at scale are what DynamoDB is designed for.

questions.prompt: What does enabling Multi AZ on RDS give you?
options: Automatic failover to a standby in another zone
questions.explanation: It is an availability feature, not a performance one.

questions.prompt: Cross region replication copies new objects to a bucket in another region.
questions.explanation: It applies to objects created after the rule is in place, which surprises people who expect a backfill.

questions.prompt: Versioning combined with MFA delete makes accidental permanent deletion much harder.
questions.explanation: The old version remains, and removing it permanently requires an extra authentication step.

questions.prompt: An encrypted EBS volume protects your data if someone gains access to the underlying physical disk.
questions.explanation: Encryption at rest addresses physical and storage layer exposure, not application level access.

questions.prompt: What problem does a message queue solve?
options: Letting one component keep working when another is slow or down
questions.explanation: Decoupling means a slow consumer creates a backlog instead of a failure.

questions.prompt: Why is deleting an SQS message a separate step from receiving it?
options: So a failed consumer does not lose the message
questions.explanation: If processing fails, the message becomes visible again instead of vanishing.

questions.prompt: What does the visibility timeout control?
options: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers
questions.explanation: If processing outlasts the timeout, another consumer can pick up the same message.

questions.prompt: What is a dead letter queue for?
options: Holding messages that repeatedly fail processing
questions.explanation: It isolates poison messages so they stop blocking the main queue.

questions.prompt: What does SNS do that SQS does not?
options: Push one message to many subscribers at once
questions.explanation: SNS is a publish and subscribe fan out, while SQS is a queue with consumers pulling from it.

questions.prompt: Why subscribe an SQS queue to an SNS topic?
options: To fan out while keeping durable, retryable delivery
questions.explanation: The topic distributes and the queue absorbs, which combines both patterns.

questions.prompt: What is EventBridge mainly used for?
options: Routing events between AWS services and applications by rule
questions.explanation: It matches events against rules and delivers them to targets.

questions.prompt: What does a Lambda function need in order to access other AWS services?
options: An execution role with the right permissions
questions.explanation: The execution role supplies temporary credentials, the same pattern as an EC2 instance role.

questions.prompt: What is a cold start?
options: The extra latency when a new execution environment is created
questions.explanation: The first request into a fresh environment pays initialisation cost that warm ones do not.

questions.prompt: Which workload is a poor fit for Lambda?
options: A short image resize on upload
A long running process that needs hours to complete
questions.explanation: Execution duration limits make long running work unsuitable.

questions.prompt: What is the operational trade off of serverless?
options: You give up direct access to the machine when debugging
questions.explanation: There is nothing to connect to, so observability has to be built in rather than added later.

questions.prompt: Why is cache invalidation considered hard?
options: Deciding when cached data has become wrong is genuinely difficult
questions.explanation: Serving stale data and clearing too aggressively are both failures, and the line between them moves.

questions.prompt: A tightly coupled system fails as a whole when one component slows down.
questions.explanation: Without a buffer between components, backpressure turns into outright failure.

questions.prompt: Standard SQS queues guarantee that messages arrive in the exact order they were sent.
questions.explanation: Ordering is only guaranteed on FIFO queues, and standard queues trade order for throughput.

questions.prompt: A cache sits between the application and the database to reduce repeated identical reads.
questions.explanation: The point is to answer common queries without touching the database every time.

questions.prompt: How many pillars does the Well Architected Framework have?
questions.explanation: The framework grew to six pillars with the addition of sustainability.

questions.prompt: Which disaster recovery strategy has the lowest cost and the slowest recovery?
questions.explanation: Backup and restore keeps nothing running, so it is cheapest and slowest to bring back.

questions.prompt: Which strategy keeps a scaled down but running copy of the environment?
questions.explanation: Warm standby runs a smaller live version that can be scaled up when needed.

questions.prompt: What is the point of writing a recovery runbook?
options: So someone else can recover the system without you
questions.explanation: A recovery that depends on one person being available is not a recovery plan.

questions.prompt: What is a spot instance?
options: Spare capacity at a large discount that can be reclaimed
questions.explanation: You get a steep discount in exchange for accepting interruption.

questions.prompt: Which pricing model suits a steady workload running for a year or more?
questions.explanation: Committing to consistent usage buys a substantial discount over on demand.

questions.prompt: What is right sizing?
options: Matching instance size to actual measured usage
questions.explanation: Metrics tell you when a resource is bigger than the workload requires.

questions.prompt: What does CloudTrail record?
options: API calls made in your account
questions.explanation: It answers who did what and when, which is the audit trail for the account.

questions.prompt: How does a WAF differ from a security group?
options: A WAF inspects application layer requests, a security group filters by IP and port
questions.explanation: One works on network attributes and the other on the content of the request.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who patches the guest operating system on EC2?
questions.explanation: AWS secures the infrastructure, and everything you run on top of it remains yours.

questions.prompt: What is the main limitation of VPC peering?
options: It is not transitive, so peered VPCs cannot route through each other
It only works in one region
questions.explanation: Non transitivity is why Transit Gateway exists for larger networks.

questions.prompt: Why do organisations use multiple AWS accounts?
options: For isolation, blast radius control and clearer billing
Because one account has a resource cap
questions.explanation: Separating environments limits how far a mistake or compromise can spread.

questions.prompt: A Direct Connect link provides a dedicated private connection rather than travelling over the public internet.
questions.explanation: That is the main reason to choose it over a VPN, along with more predictable performance.

questions.prompt: Reviewing your own architecture against the pillars will usually reveal gaps you did not notice while building it.
questions.explanation: Structured review catches what enthusiasm and momentum hide during the build.

questions.prompt: Cost is an operational concern that engineers are expected to understand, not just a finance issue.
questions.explanation: Architectural choices drive the bill, so the person making them owns part of the cost outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the most effective final stage of studying for this exam?
options: Timed practice exams with full review of wrong answers
questions.explanation: Practice exams reveal gaps and train the scenario reading that the real exam demands.

questions.prompt: Why record your practice scores by domain rather than only the total?
options: So you can target the weakest areas instead of revising evenly
questions.explanation: An even revision plan wastes time on what you already know.

questions.prompt: You are scoring sixty five percent on practice exams a week before the date. What is the sensible move?
options: Move the date and close the gaps
questions.explanation: A retake costs money and time, and moving the date is cheaper than failing.

questions.prompt: Why check the official AWS page before booking?
options: Because exam versions change and unofficial sources go stale
questions.explanation: Blogs disagree about version numbers, so the vendor page is the only reliable source.

questions.prompt: What should you do the evening before the exam?
questions.explanation: Fatigue costs more marks than one extra hour of revision gains.

questions.prompt: Why add the certification to your CV and LinkedIn the same day you pass?
options: Because momentum matters and recruiters search on it
questions.explanation: The credential only helps once it is visible where hiring people look.

questions.prompt: What does the certification actually prove to an employer?
options: That you can run production systems
That you know the services and how they fit together
questions.explanation: It signals knowledge, and your projects are what demonstrate application of it.

questions.prompt: Why is a certificate weaker on its own than a certificate plus a project?
options: Anyone can memorise answers, but a working system shows judgement
questions.explanation: The project is evidence of doing, while the exam is evidence of knowing.

questions.prompt: If you do not pass, when should you write the retake plan?
options: The same day, while the questions are fresh
questions.explanation: Your memory of which domains hurt is most accurate immediately afterwards.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a one page cheat sheet in the final days?
options: To consolidate the numbers and choices you keep forgetting
questions.explanation: Writing it is the revision, and it concentrates the facts that will not stick.

questions.prompt: Why explain a weak topic out loud as if teaching it?
options: Because stumbling reveals exactly where your understanding is thin
questions.explanation: You cannot fake fluency out loud, so the gaps become obvious.

questions.prompt: Why schedule the exam before Ramadan begins?
options: So the final push does not land in a month of reduced capacity
questions.explanation: Planning around a known low energy month is better than pretending it will not happen.

questions.prompt: Passing the exam replaces the need for hands on projects.
questions.explanation: Employers filter on the certificate and then hire on demonstrated ability, so the projects still carry the interview.

questions.prompt: Reviewing the questions you got right is less valuable than reviewing the ones you got wrong.
questions.explanation: Wrong answers show your actual gaps, though checking that a right answer was not a lucky guess is still worth doing.

questions.prompt: Reading the next exam guide immediately gives the following months a clear target.
questions.explanation: Knowing what February and March are for prevents the drift that follows finishing a big goal.
